name: Color Palette Discipline
summary: A single page should use ~6–8 core colors plus neutrals and stay at or under 10 distinct values total; every additional hue dilutes hierarchy and signals nothing new.
description: Color is a signal. When a page contains more than ~10 distinct hex values, the eye can no longer tell which colors mean something (brand, action, error) and which are incidental. A disciplined palette is role-based: 1 primary brand color, 1 accent for CTAs and emphasis, 3–4 neutrals (text, muted text, border, background, surface), and 1–2 semantic colors (success, warning/error). Hover, active, disabled, and decorative variants are derived from this small set via opacity/alpha or HSL adjustments — not introduced as new hexes. Near-duplicate values (#333 vs #363636) still count against the budget because they add cognitive noise without adding meaning. The discipline isn't aesthetic minimalism; it's making sure every color the user sees is doing a job. Map every color to a named token role: surface, surface-raised, border, text, text-muted, accent, accent-hover, success, warning, danger.
implications: Define a role-based token set before generating any UI and reuse it everywhere: surface, surface-raised, border, text, text-muted, accent, accent-hover, success, warning, danger
Keep the page at or under 10 distinct rendered colors; target ~6–8 core hues plus neutrals
Derive hover/active/disabled states with opacity/alpha (e.g. 0.8, 0.6) or lightness shifts from existing tokens, not new hexes
Express shadows as rgba() from a neutral token, not as standalone hex colors
Treat gradient stops as variations of existing tokens, not license to add new hues
Collapse near-duplicate hexes (within ~5% lightness) into a single token — #333 and #363636 are noise, not two colors
Audit generated pages by counting distinct hex values — anything over 10 has drifted
violations: A landing page with 11+ distinct hex values where several are visually indistinguishable
Introducing a new gray (#363636) when #333 is already in the palette
Hardcoding hover states as new hexes instead of deriving them from the base token
Decorative tints and gradient stops that don't map to any defined token
Shadow colors written as opaque hex values rather than rgba from a neutral
Every component author picking a slightly different gray
sources: Material Design 3 — Color roles and tonal palettes (https://m3.material.io/styles/color/roles)
Complements color-theory principles (which colors work together) with a constraint on how many should appear at once.
Raven self-audit (2026-06): generated demos repeatedly landed at 11 distinct hexes, exceeding the ~10-color hierarchy threshold (rule color/palette-size).
